name: Scalp Defects-Postaxial Polydactyly Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Scalp Defects-Postaxial Polydactyly Syndrome

criteria.description: Congenital localized scalp defect (aplasia cutis congenita)
Presence of postaxial polydactyly on hands and/or feet
Mild facial dysmorphic features including hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
Variable developmental delay or intellectual disability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital scalp defect and postaxial polydactyly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may support but is not definitive.

imaging: X-ray showing postaxial polydactyly and possible syndactyly
Brain MRI may show nonspecific findings in developmental delay cases
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern reported in some families
other: Clinical observation of scalp defect and limb anomalies is critical for diagnosis

redFlags: Large or infected scalp defect increasing risk of hemorrhage or meningitis
Congenital heart defects requiring urgent intervention
references: Orphanet: Scalp defects-postaxial polydactyly syndrome, ORPHA:1003
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Entry not available
Rimoin DL, et al. Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics. 7th ed. 2013.
